headline: Nitrogen makes up 78% of every breath—yet your body can barely use it directly
universal_truth: Being surrounded by something doesn't mean we can access it
fun_facts: Nitrogen is 78% of air but so chemically stable that most organisms can't use it directly
Lightning can 'fix' nitrogen, making it available to plants—nature's fertilizer factory
All the protein in your body requires nitrogen, yet you can't get it from breathing
discussion_questions: What are you surrounded by that you can't directly access or use?
Why might nature make something essential so difficult to obtain?
How do barriers to access create interdependence?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: With every breath, you inhale mostly nitrogen—78% of air is nitrogen. You breathe it in. You breathe it out. Unchanged. Your body is swimming in nitrogen but can barely use it. The most abundant gas is also one of the most inaccessible.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Every protein in your body requires nitrogen. Your DNA needs nitrogen. Yet you can't absorb it from the air around you. If you're surrounded by nitrogen and need it for survival, how do you get it?
cliff.prompt: How do living things get nitrogen if not from air?

options.text: Bacteria convert atmospheric nitrogen into usable forms; plants absorb it; we eat plants
options.response: Yes. Nitrogen-fixing bacteria are the hidden heroes that make nitrogen accessible to all life.

options.text: Water contains dissolved nitrogen that plants and animals can absorb
options.response: Some nitrogen is in water, but the primary pathway is through bacteria...

q1.title: The Triple Bond
q1.script: Nitrogen atoms bond to each other with a triple bond—one of the strongest in nature. This makes nitrogen gas incredibly stable, almost inert. Breaking that bond to use nitrogen requires enormous energy or specialized biology.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Triple Bond"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Bacterial Heroes
q2.script: Certain bacteria can do what we cannot—fix nitrogen. They break the triple bond and convert atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia, which plants can absorb. These bacteria live in soil and in root nodules of legumes. All protein traces back to their work.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Lightning Factories
q3.script: Lightning also fixes nitrogen—the immense energy breaks nitrogen bonds, creating nitrogen oxides that rain into soil. A single thunderstorm can fertilize acres of land. Nature has multiple systems for cracking this essential but stubborn element.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Abundance doesn't guarantee access. Nitrogen teaches that being surrounded by something doesn't mean you can use it. Value the intermediaries—the bacteria, the processes, the connectors—that make the inaccessible available.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 74. Tomorrow, we'll discover the simplest element—hydrogen. Until then, appreciate the invisible bacteria that make your proteins possible.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Access vs. Abundance - Find Your Intermediaries
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify what makes the inaccessible accessible
growTrack.activity: What valuable thing are you surrounded by but can't access directly—information, opportunity, community? Who or what could be your 'nitrogen-fixing bacteria'—the intermediary that converts potential into usable form? Seek that connector.
